title: OpenAI widens free ChatGPT for researchers but swaps Pro for Plus
excerpt: OpenAI will hand out 50,000 more free ChatGPT grants to researchers, but new grants get Plus rather than Pro. Applications open on November 23.
content_html:
OpenAI is expanding its ChatGPT for Academic Researchers programme with 50,000 new grants, each covering up to three people, and now aims to reach 200,000 researchers. New grants get ChatGPT Plus instead of Pro, and go to the first eligible applicants rather than by lottery.

OpenAI will give 50,000 more free ChatGPT grants to academic researchers, the company announced on Monday. Applications open on November 23, and grants go to the first eligible applicants instead of by lottery. Each grant covers a researcher and up to two collaborators, or up to 150,000 people in total.

There is a catch. Researchers in the pilot got ChatGPT Pro, OpenAI’s top tier, while new grants come with the cheaper Plus plan. OpenAI says most pilot users would have stayed within Plus limits, and the switch lets it reach more teams.

OpenAI now aims to reach 200,000 researchers, double the goal it set when the pilot launched in July. Back then, each researcher could invite up to four collaborators. So far, 20,000 researchers in 33 countries have joined.

OpenAI also published a study of how more than 1,800 scientists used ChatGPT in the pilot. On average, reading and learning made up 28% of their science messages, and writing 27%. Surveyed participants said the same work would have taken nearly twice as long without AI.

That figure is self-reported, and OpenAI says the study does not prove AI speeds up discovery. It also names funding, staff and lab capacity as limits on testing new ideas.

The grants are one of several OpenAI science pushes. It offers free seats on GPT-Rosalind, its biology model, to US university labs, and gave $5M to a Simons Foundation effort to help mathematicians check AI results. In August, its unreleased Astra model claimed to have solved ten open problems in maths.

Rivals are courting scientists too. Anthropic launched Claude Science, an AI workbench for labs, in June. Google DeepMind opened its science models to 200 European researchers in October.
